A.depoimento: I order the construction of two spearmen in Lisboa. I launch a double attack: a spear-led force to Santarem to exploit the counter against their knights, and archers to Evora. My capital remains guarded by two spearmen.
A.plano: Build 2 spearman. Attack Santarem with 5 spearman and 3 knight (counter bonus). Attack Evora with 4 archer. Keep 2 spearman at home.

B.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of two spearmen in Barcelona and launched an assault on the neutral village of Tarragona. With the spearmen leading the charge against the knight garrison, we should easily overwhelm them and secure the village for the crown.
B.plano: Build 2 spearmen at Barcelona. Attack Tarragona with 5 spearman, 3 archer, 2 knight. Keep 2 spearman, 1 archer, 1 knight in Barcelona for defense. Next turn, assess Girona and the newly captured Tarragona.

A.depoimento: I have ordered my armies to strike! My spearmen charge Coimbra, my knights ride to Badajoz, and my archers take Faro. At home, a new knight is forged. My remaining spearmen march to reinforce Santarem. The map will change as I claim these lands!
A.plano: Attack Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro simultaneously to expand quickly. Build a knight at Lisboa for future strength. Send the 2 spearman from Lisboa to Santarem to maintain a garrison. Next turn, assess results and push deeper into unexplored territory to reach 18 villages.

A.depoimento: I have ordered my archers to march on Porto and my knights to strike Toledo. At the same time, my villages are working hard to produce archers and knights to reinforce our ranks. The expansion has begun!
A.plano: Attack Porto with archers from Faro and Toledo with knights from Badajoz to expand my territory. Build a mix of knights and archers in all my villages to grow my army for future assaults. Next turn, I will assess the results of these attacks and plan further expansion towards Madrid and the enemy capital.

B.depoimento: I have launched attacks on the three neutral villages using knights and spearman, leveraging their counter advantages. I have also built additional knights to maintain momentum in my expansion.
B.plano: After the attacks, assess the outcomes and losses. Begin fortifying newly captured villages and plan next moves towards Madrid and beyond. Also, watch for enemy counterattacks.

A.depoimento: My armies have moved! I have sent my knights to Cordoba to capture it, and my spearmen to Salamanca to join the archers already on their way. I am reinforcing Faro and Badajoz to prepare for the next pushes. My archers in Faro will soon capture Sevilha.
A.plano: I am sending my Toledo knights to capture Cordoba, and my Coimbra spearmen to Salamanca to join the archers already marching there. I am also sending an archer from Faro to help weaken Salamanca. I am reinforcing Faro with archers from Evora and Badajoz with troops from Santarem to prepare for attacks on Sevilha and Madrid. I am building a mix of troops in all my villages to grow my army.

B.depoimento: Our armies have converged on Zaragoza. The simultaneous strike on Madrid and Huesca will begin, carving out a path to victory.
B.plano: On turn 6, order Zaragoza to send 3 knights to Madrid and 3 archers to Huesca. On turn 6, also order Tarragona to send its 3 newly built archers to Castellon for turn 7 attack on Valencia. Keep Barcelona's remaining troops for defense and future operations.

B.depoimento: This turn the crown's blade falls on Madrid and Huesca. Zaragoza splits its strength - knights for the hub of the plain, archers for the northern keep - while Tarragona's archers flow south to Castellon to prime the Valencia assault. Every village forges archers tonight; the iron runs, the arrows multiply, and King B's armies advance on all fronts.
B.plano: Turn 6: Zaragoza sends 4 knights to Madrid and 4 archers to Huesca; Tarragona sends 3 archers to Castellon. Build 1 archer at Zaragoza/Castellon/Tarragona/Girona and 3 at Barcelona. Next turn: read battle results at Madrid and Huesca, then order Castellon's archers (with its spearman) to attack Valencia, and begin scouting Salamanca/Toledo/Burgos from Madrid. Do not send Girona's knight yet - it cannot take Huesca alone.

B.depoimento: Today my armies strike twin blows: Castellon's host falls on Valencia, while Madrid's knights shatter King A's grip on Salamanca. Barcelona's knights gallop to reinforce the central spearhead, and every village works its forges to feed the advance. The enemy's western wall is crumbling, and the road to Lisboa is finally open.
B.plano: Turn 7: Castellon->Valencia (2 spear, 4 archer); Madrid->Salamanca (3 knights); Barcelona->Madrid (2 knights, arrive turn 8). Build archers at Barcelona(1), Tarragona(2), Girona(2), Castellon(2), Zaragoza(2). Turn 8: Zaragoza (2 spear, 3 archer) takes Pamplona; Madrid's 2 knights + new build take Toledo (empty) or Burgos; Valencia's force pushes to Murcia; scout Coimbra/Porto/Badajoz revealed from Salamanca. Do NOT attack Teruel yet - it needs a spearman-heavy force to counter its knights.

A.depoimento: Our armies struck at Madrid, Sevilha, and Murcia simultaneously, while reinforcements arrived in Salamanca and Toledo. The campaign to expand our territory has begun in earnest, and we hope to secure key victories to bring us closer to our goal of holding 18 villages.
A.plano: We launched a three-pronged attack on Madrid, Sevilha, and Murcia this turn to expand our territory and secure new resource-producing villages. We reinforced Salamanca with a knight from Coimbra and sent troops from Badajoz to Toledo to prepare for the next phase. Next turn, we must assess the battle results, rebuild any lost troops in Faro and Cordoba, and prepare to attack Porto and Teruel. We also need to monitor the enemy's response and be ready to defend Salamanca and Toledo from counter-attacks.

B.depoimento: This turn I held Madrid's knights in reserve and massed archers for the coming blows: Huesca's three marched to Madrid, Tarragona's one and Castellon's two reinforced Zaragoza and Valencia, and all seven of my villages produced archers. Next turn four attacks go in at once - Burgos, Salamanca, Pamplona, and Murcia - putting twelve of the twenty-four villages under my banner by the turn after.
B.plano: Turn 8 (prep only): Huesca 3 arch -> Madrid (T9); Tarragona 1 arch -> Zaragoza (T9); Castellon 2 arch -> Valencia (T9). Build 1 archer in every village (Barcelona 2). Keep Madrid's 2 knights home for defense this turn. Turn 9 attacks (all arrive T10): Madrid 2 knights+1 arch -> Burgos; Madrid 3 arch -> Salamanca; Zaragoza 5 arch -> Pamplona; Valencia 1 spear+5 arch -> Murcia. Then T10: Madrid's new archer -> Toledo (empty); Salamanca -> Coimbra; Burgos -> Vigo; Murcia -> Cordoba. Do NOT attack Teruel until 4 spearmen are gathered.

A.depoimento: King A orders his armies to strike! From Coimbra, 3 archers march to Porto to claim the neutral lands. From Toledo, an elite force of 2 knights, 1 archer, and 1 spearman marches on Madrid itself! Our troops are rebuilding in our villages, ready for the next phase of our campaign to secure the 18 villages needed for victory!
A.plano: We will launch a double attack this turn: sending 3 archers from Coimbra to conquer the neutral village of Porto, and a mixed force of 2 knights, 1 archer, and 1 spearman from Toledo to attack the enemy village of Madrid. We will also rebuild our troops across our villages to maintain our army strength. Conquering Porto will give us a new resource-producing village, while attacking Madrid will weaken the enemy and open up the path to the north.

B.depoimento: While my interior villages build archers for the push west, I commit Madrid's knights to Burgos and Zaragoza's and Valencia's archers to Pamplona and Murcia - three neutral villages fall at once. I keep Madrid's four archers at home to guard the border; Salamanca will have to wait one more turn.
B.plano: Turn 9: Madrid 2 knights -> Burgos; Zaragoza 5 archers -> Pamplona; Valencia 5 archers -> Murcia (all arrive T10). Build 2 archers in Tarragona/Girona/Castellon/Zaragoza/Huesca/Madrid, 1 in Valencia, 2 spearmen in Barcelona. Keep Madrid's 4 archers home for defense; do NOT attack Salamanca yet - it would leave Madrid naked to a counter-attack. Next turn: Madrid archers take Salamanca, then push west.

A.depoimento: Our armies are on the move. Reinforcements stream to our borders as we prepare to conquer the neutral villages of Vigo and Teruel. The attack on Madrid is imminent, and we are building a strong army to hold our new lands and press the advantage.
A.plano: Plan: This turn we build knights and archers to strengthen our armies. We send reinforcements to Porto (3 archers from Coimbra) to prepare an attack on Vigo. We gather spearmen at Toledo (2 from Badajoz, 2 spear and 1 knight from Salamanca) to attack Teruel next turn. We reinforce Cordoba (2 archers from Sevilha) and Badajoz (2 spear, 2 arch, 2 knight from Santarem) to secure the south. We also move troops from Lisbon to Santarem, and from Evora to Faro to Faro to Sevilha to consolidate our forces. Our marching army will capture Madrid. Next turn we will attack Vigo and Teruel, and then expand

A.depoimento: Turn 11 is a turning point. Our armies are on the move on all fronts. From the north, our archers march on Vigo; from the center, our spearmen charge at Teruel; from the east, our knight strikes Burgos; and from the south, our combined force assaults Murcia. Reinforcements flow to secure our borders, and our factories work overtime to fuel the campaign. The age of King A begins now!
A.plano: We are launching a massive 4-front attack this turn to expand our territory. We attack Vigo from Porto, Teruel from Toledo, Burgos from Madrid, and Murcia from Cordoba. We reinforce Porto from Coimbra, Madrid from Salamanca, Cordoba from Sevilha, and Toledo from Badajoz. We also move troops from Lisboa to Santarem, and Evora to Faro. We build archers and knights in all our villages to prepare for the next turn's consolidation and further expansion towards Zaragoza and the unexplored north.

A.depoimento: Our armies struck today: Valencia fell to Murcia's archers and knights, Zaragoza to Madrid's forces. We now hold eighteen villages! Reinforcements strengthened Burgos and Teruel, while our forges burned day and night. The enemy's capital is next in our sights.
A.plano: Attack 16 from Murcia and 17 from Madrid to reach 18 villages. Left 1 archer in Murcia, 3 spearman in Madrid. Reinforced Burgos with Vigo's archers, Teruel with Toledo's archers and knight. Built troops everywhere. Next turn: reinforce 16 and 17, continue building, watch for enemy counterattacks.

B.depoimento: Our archers stormed Burgos, breaking the enemy's western flank. Reinforcements are moving to the borders. We are building archers in every village. The march to 18 villages begins now.
B.plano: Next turn: after builds, send reinforcements to Zaragoza from Tarragona and Huesca. Send from Pamplona to Burgos to hold it. Prepare to attack Vigo from Pamplona or Burgos. Do not attack Madrid yet; gather more archers.

B.depoimento: My archers march on Madrid while the enemy's last assaults shattered against my walls. I build in every village and drive the center forward—Madrid falls, and the road west opens.
B.plano: Sent 10 archers from Zaragoza to Madrid (expect capture with ~5 survivors). Reinforced Zaragoza with 4 archers each from Tarragona and Huesca. Built 1 archer in every village (2 in Valencia). Next turn: reinforce Madrid, then attack Salamanca [7] from Madrid. Do not strip Valencia too far; watch Teruel and Murcia. Prepare spearmen for Burgos (knight-heavy).

A.depoimento: I am launching a decisive attack on Madrid from Salamanca and Toledo, while reinforcing my borders and building up my army across the kingdom. This turn is about securing Madrid and setting up for the conquest of Zaragoza and Pamplona next turn to reach the 18-village threshold.
A.plano: Conquer Madrid this turn using Salamanca and Toledo. Reinforce Burgos with Vigo, Salamanca with Porto and Coimbra, Toledo with Cordoba. Build troops in all villages to prepare for the next wave of attacks (Zaragoza and Pamplona next turn). Do not attack Teruel or Valencia yet as they are too strong.

A.depoimento: This turn we attacked Castellon and Pamplona to expand our territory. We sent reinforcements to our border villages and built troops across our realm. Our armies are preparing for the next attacks on Zaragoza and Valencia. We aim to secure 18 villages and then push for total victory.
A.plano: Attack Castellon from Teruel and Pamplona from Burgos to reach 18 villages. Reinforce Madrid, Teruel, Murcia, and Burgos with interior troops. Build troops everywhere. Next turn, attack Zaragoza from Madrid and Valencia from Teruel/Murcia to secure 20 villages. Hold and reinforce new conquests. Do not attack Barcelona yet.

B.depoimento: King B's forces conquered Madrid, striking at the enemy's heart. We consolidated our armies, sending archers and spearmen to Castellon to form a massive strike force. The path to Teruel opens next turn. Our villages are building more archers to sustain the campaign.
B.plano: We attacked Madrid from Zaragoza with all troops. We sent reinforcements from Tarragona and Valencia to Castellon, and from Barcelona to Tarragona, Girona to Huesca, Huesca to Zaragoza. Next turn, attack Teruel from Castellon with the combined army. Also, after taking Madrid, consider attacking Salamanca or Toledo. Build archers at all villages.

A.depoimento: We launch a massive offensive on Zaragoza and Valencia from our border villages. Our knights lead the charge, aiming to break the enemy lines and secure these key territories. With our combined forces, we hope to overwhelm the enemy and expand our empire.
A.plano: Attack Zaragoza from Madrid and Valencia from Teruel and Murcia to conquer both and reach 19 villages. Build troops in all villages to replenish losses and prepare for the next phase. Next turn, hold and reinforce the new conquests, and plan the assault on Castellon. Do not attack Barcelona yet.
